_about: VA programs that pay for work done in a veteran's home, for the 'Who pays for it' section of guide.vethomeguard.org/contractors/. Each names the official page it was read on. trades are directory trade keys whose businesses can do the work; caregiving programs have none because the directory does not list caregivers yet.

programs.label: HISA grant (Home Improvements and Structural Alterations)
programs.pays_for: Medically needed changes to the home a veteran lives in: permanent ramps, roll-in showers, wider doorways, railings, and the electrical or plumbing work needed for home medical equipment. Not routine repairs, stair glides or new construction.
programs.who: Veterans enrolled in VA health care whose VA clinician writes up the need. The amount depends on service-connected status.
programs.how: Ask the Prosthetic and Sensory Aids Service at your VA medical center. VA wants a written estimate that separates labor, materials, permits and inspections, and approves it before work starts, so get your bids first.
programs.source: VA Prosthetic and Sensory Aids Service: HISA

programs.label: Adapted housing grants (SAH and SHA)
programs.pays_for: Building, buying or changing a home so a veteran with certain service-connected disabilities can live there more independently. Bigger projects than HISA.
programs.who: Veterans and service members with qualifying service-connected disabilities, such as loss of use of limbs, blindness or severe burns.
programs.how: Apply through VA. Your builder or contractor’s plans and costs are part of the review, so line up bids early.
programs.source: VA.gov: Disability housing grants for veterans

programs.label: Veteran-Directed Care
programs.pays_for: A monthly budget the veteran or family manages to hire their own in-home help, often a spouse, adult child, friend or neighbor, and to buy approved goods and services.
programs.who: Veterans enrolled in VA health care who need help with daily activities and would otherwise be at risk of a nursing home. Not offered at every VA.
programs.how: Ask your VA social worker or care team whether it is offered where you live.
programs.source: VA Geriatrics and Extended Care: Veteran-Directed Care

programs.label: Homemaker and Home Health Aide care
programs.pays_for: A trained aide who comes to the home to help with bathing, dressing, meals, errands and other daily tasks. Aides work for agencies under contract with VA.
programs.who: Veterans enrolled in VA health care with a clinical need. A copay may apply depending on service-connected status.
programs.how: Ask your VA primary care team or social worker for a referral.
programs.source: VA Geriatrics and Extended Care: Homemaker and Home Health Aide Care
